description: Chart 15 — Venue density under the network, inner Melbourne. The zoomed synthesis: venues are binned offline into a hexagonal tessellation (venue_hexbins_melbourne.topojson, built by tools/build-hexbins.mjs from venues_web.csv over the same Melbourne frame, lon 144.75–145.35 / lat −37.92 to −37.67) and drawn as projected hexagons underneath the train + tram routes. A true hexbin tiles seamlessly and stays aligned with the route layer at any width, which fixed-size circles or point marks cannot. The message: venue concentration piles up along the tram grid and radial train lines, instead of only identifying Melbourne on a statewide grid. Proximity, not service. Routes are drawn on top; the stop mesh is dropped so the density layer reads. Data: venue_hexbins_melbourne.topojson over pt_routes_melbourne.topojson and sa2_melbourne.topojson.

title.text: Venue density hugs the network — inner Melbourne
subtitle: The heatmap belongs here: density piles up on the tram grid and train corridors,
not just on 'Melbourne' as a whole.

layer.description: Base: inner-Melbourne SA2 boundaries (shared clipped base).

Venue density as a hexagonal tessellation, binned offline from venues_web.csv (tools/build-hexbins.mjs) so the cells are real geographic polygons that tile seamlessly. The venue count per hex is encoded by a single sequential warm fill — size is fixed because the cells tile, so this is colour-only, no size channel.
Train + tram routes, Melbourne-clipped, drawn on top of the binned venue-density layer so the public-transport representation is the visible overlay.
